sc: 3-week-old with 38.2 °C who looks well → Admit: full septic screen + IV antibiotics
18-month-old, fever, no focus, well → Urine dipstick and culture (UTI)
Fever with a non-blanching rash → Meningococcal sepsis: ceftriaxone now
f: Fever ≥ 38 °C · FUO: fever > 2–3 weeks with no cause after 1 week of tests
Cannot drink or breastfeed · vomits everything · convulsions · lethargic or unconscious · stiff neck
Age < 3 months = high risk · look for a focus: ears, throat, chest, urine, skin, joints, neck stiffness · malaria test in endemic areas
Common infections (UTI, TB) · malaria · typhoid, brucellosis, kala-azar · Kawasaki · JIA · leukaemia
Paracetamol 15 mg/kg 6-hourly · ibuprofen 10 mg/kg 6–8-hourly · treat the cause
Reassess the child, not the thermometer: activity, feeding, perfusion · a well-looking child after paracetamol is reassuring
trap: Aspirin is not used for fever (Reye syndrome) · fever + hepatosplenomegaly + pancytopenia in an endemic area → kala-azar (and leukaemia) · do not give steroids "to bring the fever down"
